feedback.problem: Use Pascal's triangle to determine the value of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{4}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the value of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{4}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $5$ and position $4$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The value located in row $5$ and position $4$ is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & 1 \\  &  &  &  &  &  & 1 &  & 1 \\  &  &  &  &  & 1 &  & 2 &  & 1 \\  &  &  &  & 1 &  & 3 &  & 3 &  & 1 \\  &  &  & 1 &  & 4 &  & 6 &  & 4 &  & 1 \\  &  & 1 &  & 5 &  & 10 &  & 10 &  & 5 &  & 1 \\  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{4})=5.$
